newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria, Tunisia take "new step" in relations.
newsitem.headline: Algeria, Tunisia take "new step" in relations.

text.p: Algerian Interior Minister Mustapha Ben Mansour said on Monday his country and neighbouring Tunisia had "taken a new step towards consolidating cooperation", the official Algerian news agency APS reported.
Ben Mansour was speaking after signing a note on strengthening bilateral relations with visiting Tunisian Interior Minister Mohamed Jegham.
Tunisia and Algeria are both members of the Arab Maghreb Union, along with Morocco, Libya and Mauritania, but relations have in the past been strained.
"The two countries must pursue this joint effort by applying agreements reached between officials of the two countries," APS reported the Algerian minister as saying.
Jegham, who arrived in Algiers on Saturday, met Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Monday.

APS said Jegham reiterated to Zeroual "the willingness and determination of Tunisia to reinforce cooperation with Algeria in all fields, notably those linked to security and the stability of the two countries."

Algerian security forces have for the past five years been engaged in a conflict with Moslem fundamentalists, including clashes near the border with Tunisia, in which about 60,000 people have been killed.
